children: High Density Data Centre Ltd, a unit of India's Adani Group, has received approval to invest Rs 1.04 lakh crore to develop a 1 gigawatt data centre park in Odisha.

The project, cleared by the High-Level Clearance Authority chaired by Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, is among the largest proposed investments in the rapidly expanding data centre industry as demand for computing capacity rises with the adoption of artificial intelligence.
The Odisha government has earmarked about 250 acres at Naraj for the facility.
The proposed investment is just below the Rs 1.08 lakh crore project announced by Reliance Industries in Andhra Pradesh, which includes an AI data centre and a cable landing station.
Adani's data centre business, AdaniConneX, already operates a facility in Chennai and is developing projects in Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad.

The Odisha government also approved three other data centre and AI-related projects with a combined investment of Rs 38,391 crore, taking the total investment cleared across the four projects to about Rs 1.42 trillion.
HCLTech has received approval for a Rs 14,257 crore AI-optimised data centre in Khordha, in partnership with Indian AI company Sarvam AI.

Sentraforge AI, a joint venture between Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Ltd and GVPR Engineers Ltd, plans to invest Rs 22,634 crore in a 120 MW sovereign AI campus and global capability centre in Puri.
RKD Construction has also received clearance for a Rs 1,500 crore data centre in Cuttack district.
The state has identified a 140-acre site at Tangiapada near Bhubaneswar's Info Valley for a data centre hub that will accommodate the HCLTech and Sentraforge projects.
